rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections – just cause required to terminate tenancy
rules.requirement: A San Diego landlord may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault cause (such as nonpayment, lease breach after a written notice to fix it, nuisance or criminal activity) or a listed no-fault cause (owner or close-relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, a government order, demolition or substantial remodel). For a curable violation, the landlord must first give written notice and a chance to cure. Termination notices must state the cause and be reported to the San Diego Housing Commission.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; owner move-in requires 12 months' occupancy within 90 days; 5-year right of first refusal after no-fault eviction
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego with a tenancy of more than 30 days (not fixed-term leases of 3 months or less). Housing whose certificate of occupancy was issued within the previous 15 years is exempt.
rules.exemptions: Hotels/short-term occupancy; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 vouchers not exempt); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; care facilities and dormitories; units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with a resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family home renting up to two bedrooms/ADUs; owner-occupied duplex; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years; separately alienable units (single-family homes, condos) whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, if tenants get the required written exemption notice.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.penalty: Wrongful eviction liability of at least three times actual economic damages; injunctive relief, punitive damages, discretionary attorney's fees; noncompliant termination notices are void; City civil and criminal enforcement.

exemption_tests.description: Certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes)
Two units in one structure, with the landlord living in one as principal residence since the start of the tenancy
Separately alienable unit (single-family home or condo) whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with the required written exemption notice given to tenants
Housing restricted by deed or agreement as affordable, or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 vouchers do not trigger this exemption)
Tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with a landlord who lives there as principal residence

rules.title: San Diego relocation assistance for no-fault terminations
rules.requirement: If a San Diego landlord ends a tenancy for a no-fault reason, the landlord must pay relocation assistance of two months' actual rent, or three months' if the tenant is a senior (62+) or disabled. The landlord may pay directly within 15 days of the notice or waive the same amount of rent, regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors 62+ or disabled tenants)
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault terminations of tenancies in residential rental property covered by San Diego Mun. Code Ch. 9, Art. 8, Div. 7. Housing whose certificate of occupancy was issued within the previous 15 years is exempt.
rules.exemptions: Same as the Division's exemptions (§ 98.0703). No assistance is owed if a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault for the condition behind a vacate order.
rules.quoted_span:
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in 
effect
rules.penalty: Liability of at least three times the required relocation assistance plus actual economic damages (§ 98.0709(e)); termination notice void.

exemption_tests.description: Certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes)
Separately alienable unit with a non-corporate landlord and the required written exemption notice
Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8 vouchers)

rules.title: California statewide rent increase cap (referenced in San Diego tenant notice)
rules.requirement: California law limits how much rent can be increased for covered units; see Civil Code section 1947.12.
rules.quoted_span: California law limits the amount your rent can be increased.

notes:
The source is the official San Diego Municipal Code, Ch. 9, Art. 8, Div. 7 (O-21647, effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769, effective 2024-03-28).
1. Main rule: the just cause requirement (§ 98.0704) and its notice rules (§ 98.0706(a)-(b)) are recorded as one rule. The no-fault relocation assistance (§ 98.0706(c)) is a separate record.
2. displaces_state_rule is set to true because the ordinance says it requires just cause consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 and adds protections beyond it. Under § 1946.2(g), a local ordinance governs only if it is more protective than state law. A reviewer may want to confirm the City's findings on this point.
3. The 15-year certificate-of-occupancy exemption is a rolling test, so it is entered as min_building_age_years = 15.
4. Left out as out of scope:
   - Buyout agreement rules (§ 98.0707)
   - Retaliation ban (§ 98.0708)
   - Duty to give tenants the Tenant Protection notice and Guide (§ 98.0705)
   - Commission reporting portal timing
5. The California rent-cap record (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12) comes only from a short mention in the required tenant notice. It has no details, so its confidence is low.
6. Quoted spans were kept within single lines of the PDF text so they match the document exactly.
